name: Cable crossover fly
form_cues: Set pulleys high and take a staggered stance.
Keep a soft bend in the elbows throughout.
Sweep hands down and together in a hugging arc.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into a press.
Letting the handles yank the shoulders back at the top.
safety: Use a weight you can control at the stretch to protect the shoulder joint.
notes: High-to-low angle biases the lower chest.

name: Mid-height cable fly
form_cues: Set pulleys at chest height.
Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
Squeeze the chest hard as the handles meet.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and losing the arc.
safety: Stop the stretch where the shoulders still feel stable.
notes: Targets the middle of the chest.

name: Low-to-high cable fly
form_cues: Set pulleys at the lowest notch.
Scoop the handles up to chin height.
Keep chest proud and elbows softly bent.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a front raise.
Arching the lower back to lift the weight.
safety: Keep the load light enough that the shoulders don't roll forward.
notes: Biases the upper (clavicular) chest.

name: Kneeling cable crossover
form_cues: Kneel tall in the middle of the crossover.
Brace your core so the hips don't move.
Bring hands together in front of your belly button.
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso to cheat the weight.
safety: Use a mat under the knees.
notes: Kneeling removes leg drive and keeps the work strict.

name: Single-arm cable fly
form_cues: Stand side-on with the handle at shoulder height.
Sweep the arm across past the midline.
Keep hips and shoulders square.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to finish the rep.
safety: Control the return so the shoulder isn't pulled into a deep stretch.
notes: Crossing past the midline gives a stronger peak contraction.

name: Standing cable chest press
form_cues: Set pulleys at chest height and step forward.
Press the handles straight out and slightly together.
Brace your core so you don't lean.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows straight out to the sides.
safety: Use a staggered stance for balance.

name: Single-arm cable chest press
form_cues: Stand facing away with the handle at chest height.
Press forward without letting the torso twist.
Use the opposite leg forward for a stable base.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips to push the weight.
safety: Start light; the anti-rotation demand is bigger than it looks.

name: Low-to-high cable press
form_cues: Set pulleys low and stand in a split stance.
Press up and out at about 30 degrees.
Finish with hands at eye level.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a shoulder press.
safety: Keep ribs down to protect the lower back.

name: Flat bench cable press
form_cues: Place the bench between low pulleys.
Press up and slightly together over the chest.
Lower until hands are level with your chest.
common_mistakes: Bench not centred so tension is uneven.
safety: Have handles in place before lying down so you don't twist to grab them.
notes: Constant tension compared to dumbbells.

name: Incline bench cable press
form_cues: Set the bench to 30–45 degrees between low pulleys.
Press up over the upper chest.
Keep shoulder blades pinned to the bench.
common_mistakes: Bench set too steep, turning it into a shoulder press.
safety: Grab handles before reclining to avoid twisting under load.

name: Flat bench cable fly
form_cues: Lie on a bench between low pulleys.
Open the arms wide with soft elbows.
Hug the handles together over your chest.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hands too low below the bench.
safety: Keep the stretch controlled to protect the shoulder.
notes: Keeps tension at the top, unlike dumbbell flies.

name: Incline bench cable fly
form_cues: Set the bench to about 30 degrees between low pulleys.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
Bring hands together over the upper chest.
safety: Use moderate weight; deep stretch under load stresses the shoulder.

name: Decline cable fly
form_cues: Set a decline bench between low pulleys.
Lock in your feet before taking the handles.
Sweep the handles together over the lower chest.
common_mistakes: Letting the head hang off the bench.
safety: Avoid if lying head-down makes you dizzy or you have high blood pressure.
notes: High-to-low standing fly is an easier substitute.

name: Wide-grip lat pulldown
form_cues: Grip the bar just outside shoulder width.
Pull your elbows down toward your back pockets.
Bring the bar to the top of your chest.
common_mistakes: Leaning way back and turning it into a row.
Pulling with the arms only and shrugging.
safety: Lock thighs under the pad and control the bar on the way up.

name: Close-grip lat pulldown
form_cues: Attach a V-handle and sit tall.
Lean back slightly and pull to the upper chest.
Squeeze the shoulder blades down and back.
common_mistakes: Rounding forward on the way up.
safety: Keep the movement smooth; don't let the stack slam.

name: Reverse-grip lat pulldown
form_cues: Grip the bar palms-up at shoulder width.
Drive the elbows down to your sides.
Touch the bar to your upper chest.
common_mistakes: Curling the bar down with the biceps.
safety: Avoid a very narrow grip if your wrists or elbows complain.

name: Neutral-grip lat pulldown
form_cues: Hold the parallel handles palms facing each other.
Pull the elbows straight down to your ribs.
Pause briefly with the chest up.
common_mistakes: Partial reps without a full stretch.
safety: Shoulder-friendly grip; good if wide grip bothers your shoulders.

name: Behind-the-neck lat pulldown
form_cues: Lean your head slightly forward under the bar.
Pull only to the base of your skull.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
common_mistakes: Jutting the head forward to clear the bar.
Using heavy weight with poor shoulder mobility.
safety: Only use if you have good shoulder external rotation; skip it if it pinches.
notes: Front pulldowns train the same muscles with less shoulder stress.

name: Single-arm lat pulldown
form_cues: Use a single D-handle and sit tall.
Pull the elbow down to your hip.
Let the arm reach high for a full stretch.
safety: Keep the free hand on the thigh pad for stability.
notes: Great for fixing side-to-side imbalances.

name: Kneeling single-arm cable pulldown
form_cues: Set the pulley high and kneel in front of it.
Drive the elbow down toward your hip.
Keep ribs down and hips square.
common_mistakes: Leaning sideways to finish the rep.
Pulling the hand past the shoulder line.
safety: Use a mat under the knee.

name: Cross-body cable lat pulldown
form_cues: Set the pulley high and reach across to the opposite handle.
Pull the elbow down and in toward your side.
Feel a big stretch at the top.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a straight-arm pulldown.
safety: Use a weight you can control through the full arc.
notes: Works well in a cable crossover with the far pulley.

name: Straight-arm pulldown
form_cues: Hinge slightly with arms long and soft elbows.
Sweep the bar down to your thighs.
Keep the chest up and ribs down.
common_mistakes: Bending elbows into a tricep pushdown.
Using the hips to swing the weight.
safety: Keep the weight moderate; it's a feel exercise.
notes: Great lat warm-up before pull-ups or pulldowns.

name: Rope straight-arm pulldown
form_cues: Hinge forward with arms long.
Pull the rope to your hips and flare the ends apart.
Return slowly until you feel the lats stretch.
safety: Keep the spine neutral as you hinge.
notes: The rope allows a slightly longer range than the bar.

name: Lying cable pullover
form_cues: Lie on a bench with head toward a low pulley.
Arms long, pull the bar over to your thighs.
Keep your lower back flat on the bench.
common_mistakes: Arching the back at the stretch.
safety: Keep the stretch overhead within a pain-free range.

name: Kayak row
form_cues: Hold the bar wide and pull one end down to the hip.
Rotate slightly toward the working side.
Alternate sides like paddling a kayak.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and losing control of the bar.
Not returning to full stretch between sides.
safety: Keep the movement controlled; the bar can swing.

name: Seated cable row
form_cues: Sit tall with a slight bend in the knees.
Pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Squeeze shoulder blades together, then reach forward.
common_mistakes: Rocking back and forth with the torso.
Rounding the back on the return.
safety: Keep a neutral spine; don't let the stack pull you into a rounded back.

name: Wide-grip seated cable row
form_cues: Hold a lat bar wide, palms down.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, elbows out.
Pinch the shoulder blades together.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to finish the rep.
safety: Keep the torso steady; don't swing.
notes: Elbows-out pulling biases the upper back and rear delts.

name: Reverse-grip seated cable row
form_cues: Grip a straight bar palms-up at shoulder width.
Drive elbows back close to your sides.
Pull to the belly button.
safety: Use a grip width that's comfortable for your wrists.

name: Single-arm seated cable row
form_cues: Sit tall holding one D-handle.
Pull the elbow back past your ribs.
Allow a little reach forward for a stretch.
common_mistakes: Twisting a lot to move the weight.
safety: Brace the free hand on the platform or thigh.

name: Standing cable row
form_cues: Set the pulley at chest height.
Stand in a quarter squat with chest up.
Row to the lower ribs, then reach long.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to use body weight.
safety: Hold a stable athletic stance so you don't get pulled forward.

name: Single-arm standing cable row
form_cues: Stand in a split stance, opposite leg forward.
Row the handle to your hip.
Keep the hips facing the machine.
safety: Start light to learn the anti-rotation control.

name: Bent-over cable row
form_cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, knees soft.
Row the bar to your belly button.
Keep the torso angle fixed.
safety: Keep the spine neutral; skip if your lower back is irritated.

name: Cable high row
form_cues: Set the pulley high and kneel or sit facing it.
Pull handles toward your upper chest, elbows wide.
Squeeze shoulder blades down and together.
safety: Use a mat if kneeling.

name: Single-arm high cable row
form_cues: Set the pulley high and stand in a split stance.
Row the elbow down and back toward the hip.
Reach up fully between reps.
safety: Keep the shoulder down away from the ear.

name: Cable shrug
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley holding the bar.
Shrug the shoulders straight up to the ears.
Pause, then lower slowly.
safety: Keep the neck relaxed and chin neutral.

name: Single-arm cable shrug
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low pulley holding one handle.
Shrug up and slightly back.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
safety: Keep the neck neutral and avoid tilting the head.
notes: The angled pull lines up well with the upper trap fibres.

name: Rope face pull
form_cues: Set the rope at forehead height.
Pull toward your face, splitting the rope.
Finish with hands beside your ears, thumbs back.
common_mistakes: Pulling to the chest instead of the face.
Using heavy weight and leaning back.
safety: Keep it light and smooth; it's a shoulder-health move.
notes: Great for posture and shoulder health; kneeling version reduces cheating.

name: Cable lateral raise
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low pulley, handle in the far hand.
Raise the arm out to shoulder height.
Lead with the elbow and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Raising above shoulder height with shrugged traps.
safety: Keep the weight light enough for strict reps.
notes: Constant tension at the bottom, where dumbbells go slack.

name: Cable lean-away lateral raise
form_cues: Hold the machine and lean away from a low pulley.
Raise the arm out to the side.
Keep a slight bend in the elbow.
common_mistakes: Changing the lean during the set.
Letting the wrist lead above the elbow.
safety: Keep a firm grip on the machine with the free hand.
notes: Leaning away increases tension at the bottom of the range.

name: Behind-the-back cable lateral raise
form_cues: Stand side-on with the cable running behind your back.
Raise the arm out to the side.
Keep the torso still and upright.
safety: Keep it light; the start position stretches the shoulder.
notes: An ankle strap around the wrist removes grip from the movement.

name: Two-arm cable lateral raise
form_cues: Stand in the middle of a crossover with low pulleys.
Hold opposite handles crossed in front.
Raise both arms out to shoulder height.
safety: Use light weights and focus on smooth tempo.

name: Cable Y-raise
form_cues: Hold opposite low handles crossed in front of you.
Raise the arms up and out into a Y.
Stop when arms are just above head height.
safety: Keep it light; stop if you feel pinching overhead.
notes: Good for upper-back and shoulder balance.

name: Cable front raise
form_cues: Stand facing away from a low pulley.
Raise the attachment to eye level with straight arms.
Lower slowly without swinging.
safety: Keep the core tight to protect the lower back.

name: Single-arm cable front raise
form_cues: Stand facing away with the cable between your legs.
Raise the arm straight to eye level.
Keep the torso square.
safety: Keep the weight light; front delts already get lots of pressing work.

name: Reverse cable fly
form_cues: Set pulleys at shoulder height and cross the cables.
Pull arms out wide with soft elbows.
Keep the chest tall and don't shrug.
common_mistakes: Squeezing shoulder blades too hard and using traps.
Bending the elbows into a row.
safety: Use light weight; rear delts are small muscles.
notes: Hold the cable ends directly or use handles.

name: Single-arm cable reverse fly
form_cues: Stand side-on with the pulley at shoulder height.
Reach across and pull the arm out wide.
Stop when the arm is in line with your body.
safety: Keep the movement smooth and light.

name: Bent-over cable rear delt raise
form_cues: Hinge forward with crossed low cables.
Raise arms out to the sides.
Hold the hinge without bouncing.
safety: Keep a neutral spine; use a bench for chest support if needed.

name: Cable rear delt row
form_cues: Set the pulley at chest height.
Row with elbows high and wide.
Pull to the upper chest, not the face.
safety: Keep shoulders down and away from ears.

name: Cable upright row
form_cues: Hold the bar shoulder-width at a low pulley.
Lead with the elbows up to chest height.
Keep the bar close to your body.
common_mistakes: Pulling the hands higher than the elbows.
safety: Stop at chest height if you feel shoulder pinching.

name: Rope cable upright row
form_cues: Hold the rope ends at a low pulley.
Pull up and apart, elbows leading.
Stop at chest height.
safety: The rope lets wrists move freely; stop if shoulders pinch.

name: Cable shoulder press
form_cues: Set pulleys low and stand or sit between them.
Press the handles overhead.
Keep ribs down and avoid arching.
common_mistakes: Letting elbows drift behind the body.
safety: Brace your core so the lower back doesn't arch.
notes: Single-arm half-kneeling version adds core work.

name: Cable external rotation
form_cues: Set the pulley at elbow height, stand side-on.
Keep elbow tucked, rotate the forearm outward.
Return slowly.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow drift away from the side.
safety: Use very light weight; stop if you feel sharp pain.
notes: Place a rolled towel between elbow and side.

name: Cable internal rotation
form_cues: Stand side-on with the pulley at elbow height.
Keep the elbow at your side.
Rotate the forearm across your stomach.
safety: Light weight only; this is a rehab and prehab move.

name: Cable bar curl
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley.
Keep elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl to shoulder height and lower slowly.
safety: Use a weight you can lower under control.
notes: An EZ bar is easier on the wrists.

name: Rope hammer curl
form_cues: Hold the rope with palms facing each other.
Curl up keeping elbows still.
Lower all the way down.
safety: Keep wrists straight, not bent back.

name: Single-arm cable curl
form_cues: Hold a D-handle at a low pulley.
Curl with the palm turning up.
Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.
safety: Keep the shoulder still.

name: High cable curl
form_cues: Stand between high pulleys, arms out to the sides.
Curl the handles toward your ears.
Keep upper arms level with the shoulders.
safety: Use light weight; shoulders are in an exposed position.
notes: Hits the biceps in a shortened, peak-contraction position.

name: Bayesian cable curl
form_cues: Stand facing away from a low pulley.
Let the arm hang slightly behind you.
Curl without letting the elbow drift forward.
common_mistakes: Bringing the elbow forward to finish.
safety: Ease into the stretch if your front shoulder feels tight.
notes: Trains the biceps in a lengthened position.

name: Cable preacher curl
form_cues: Set a preacher bench in front of a low pulley.
Rest the upper arms flat on the pad.
Curl up and lower to nearly straight.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad.
safety: Don't snap the elbows straight at the bottom.
notes: Single-handle version works one arm at a time.

name: Lying cable curl
form_cues: Lie on your back with feet toward a low pulley.
Keep upper arms on the floor.
Curl the bar toward your forehead.
safety: Use a mat for comfort.
notes: Locks out body swing for very strict reps.

name: Cable reverse curl
form_cues: Grip the bar palms down.
Curl up with wrists straight.
Lower slowly.
safety: Use an EZ bar if straight-bar wrists ache.

name: Cross-body cable hammer curl
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low pulley.
Curl the handle across toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep the elbow tight to the side.
safety: Keep wrist neutral.

name: Cable concentration curl
form_cues: Kneel or sit with the elbow braced on the thigh.
Curl the handle up slowly.
Squeeze hard at the top.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the thigh.
safety: Choose a weight you can control.

name: Cable drag curl
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley.
Drag the bar up your body, elbows going back.
Keep the bar touching your torso.
safety: Stand close so the cable runs vertically.

name: Cable wrist curl
form_cues: Kneel or sit with forearms on a bench, palms up.
Let the bar roll to your fingers.
Curl the wrists up and squeeze.
safety: Use light weight; wrist tendons get sore easily.
notes: Flip palms down for a reverse wrist curl.

name: Rope pushdown
form_cues: Set the rope high and pin elbows to your sides.
Push down and spread the rope at the bottom.
Let forearms rise only to parallel.
common_mistakes: Leaning over to use body weight.
safety: Keep wrists neutral and shoulders down.

name: Straight-bar pushdown
form_cues: Grip the bar palms down, shoulder width.
Elbows tight, push until arms are straight.
Control the bar back up.
safety: Avoid locking out hard if elbows ache.

name: V-bar pushdown
form_cues: Hold the V-handle with thumbs up top.
Keep elbows at your sides.
Press down to full extension.
safety: Use a weight you can lower slowly.
notes: Usually allows the heaviest loads of the pushdown variations.

name: Reverse-grip tricep pushdown
form_cues: Grip the bar palms up.
Keep elbows locked in place at your sides.
Push down until arms are straight.
safety: Keep it light; wrists are in a weaker position.

name: Single-arm cable pushdown
form_cues: Hold a D-handle from a high pulley.
Pin the elbow and press down to straight.
Control the return.
safety: Keep the shoulder down and still.
notes: Underhand or overhand grip both work.

name: Overhead rope extension
form_cues: Face away from the pulley, rope behind your head.
Keep elbows pointing forward.
Extend until arms are straight.
safety: Use a split stance and brace to protect the lower back.
notes: A straight bar works too; stretches the long head.

name: Single-arm overhead cable extension
form_cues: Face away from a low pulley, handle behind the head.
Keep the upper arm by your ear.
Extend up until straight.
safety: Ease into the bottom stretch.

name: Cable tricep kickback
form_cues: Hinge forward holding a low cable.
Keep upper arm parallel to the floor.
Straighten the arm back and squeeze.
safety: Keep a flat back in the hinge.

name: Cross-body cable tricep extension
form_cues: Hold opposite high cables crossed in front of your face.
Extend arms out and down to the sides.
Keep elbows at shoulder height.
safety: Use light weight; focus on squeezing the triceps.
notes: Can be done one arm at a time.

name: Lying cable tricep extension
form_cues: Lie on a bench, head toward a low pulley.
Upper arms angled slightly back.
Extend the bar up, bend back toward your forehead.
safety: Control the bar near the head.
notes: Constant tension version of a skull crusher.

name: Cable glute kickback
form_cues: Attach the strap and hold the frame.
Kick the leg back with a slight knee bend.
Squeeze the glute without arching your back.
safety: Keep core braced to protect the lower back.

name: Straight-leg cable hip extension
form_cues: Face the pulley with the strap on one ankle.
Keep the leg straight and push it back.
Stop before your lower back arches.
safety: Hold the frame for balance.

name: Cable donkey kickback
form_cues: Get on all fours facing a low pulley.
Drive the heel up toward the ceiling.
Keep the hips square and back flat.
safety: Use a mat for your knees.

name: Cable fire hydrant
form_cues: On all fours, side-on to a low pulley.
Lift the bent knee out to the side.
Keep the torso still.
safety: Light weight; slow control matters more.

name: Standing cable hip abduction
form_cues: Stand side-on with the strap on the far ankle.
Lift the leg out to the side.
Keep the toes pointing forward.
safety: Hold the frame for balance.

name: Standing cable hip adduction
form_cues: Stand side-on with the strap on the near ankle.
Pull the leg across your body.
Return slowly to the start.
common_mistakes: Too big a stretch out to the side.
safety: Ease into the outward stretch to avoid groin strains.

name: Standing cable hip flexion
form_cues: Face away from a low pulley, strap on the ankle.
Drive the knee up to hip height.
Keep standing tall.
safety: Hold the frame for balance.
notes: Useful for runners and kicking sports.

name: Standing cable hamstring curl
form_cues: Face the pulley with the strap on the ankle.
Curl the heel toward the glute.
Keep the thigh still.
common_mistakes: Moving the thigh forward and back.
safety: Hold the frame and keep hips steady.
notes: Home-gym substitute for a leg curl machine.

name: Cable pull-through
form_cues: Face away from a low pulley, rope between legs.
Push hips back with a flat back.
Drive hips forward and squeeze the glutes.
safety: Walk far enough out that the stack doesn't touch at the top.
notes: Good way to learn the hip hinge.

name: Cable Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Stand close to a low pulley holding the bar.
Push the hips back, bar sliding down the thighs.
Stand up by squeezing the glutes.
safety: Stop at mid-shin or when your back starts to round.

name: Single-leg cable Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Hold the handle in the hand opposite the standing leg.
Hinge forward as the free leg goes back.
Keep hips level.
safety: Touch the frame with the free hand for balance if needed.

name: Cable squat
form_cues: Hold the attachment at chest, lean back slightly.
Sit down between your heels.
Drive up through the whole foot.
safety: Keep the cable taut and stand far enough back.
notes: The counterbalance helps beginners squat deeper.

name: Cable sumo squat
form_cues: Stand wide over a low pulley, toes out.
Squat straight down with the chest up.
Push knees out over toes.
safety: Stand on boxes for a deeper range if the stack hits the floor.

name: Cable split squat
form_cues: Stand in a long split stance holding low cables.
Drop the back knee straight down.
Push through the front heel.
safety: Keep the back knee off the floor.

name: Cable reverse lunge
form_cues: Face the pulley holding a handle at the chest.
Step back and lower the back knee.
Drive through the front foot to return.
safety: Move slowly and keep balance.

name: Cable lateral lunge
form_cues: Stand side-on holding a handle at the chest.
Step out wide and sit back into the hip.
Push back to the start.
common_mistakes: Knee travelling past the toes inward.
safety: Keep the trailing leg straight and the heel down.
